statement: For every rounding model with nonnegative relative error bound u and every finite nonempty ordered binary tree T of real pairs, if (depth(T)+1)u < 1, rounding each leaf product and each internal-node addition according to T yields the exact sum of a tree of perturbed exact products of the same shape. Each exact product x is replaced by a real y with |y-x| <= ((depth(T)+1)u/(1-(depth(T)+1)u))|x|. This is a perturbation of the products, not an asserted perturbation of their individual factors.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every model m in Research.FloatingPoint.Model and every T in Tree(R x R), set u=m.u and d=depth(T) in the natural numbers. If (d+1)u < 1, with d+1 cast to R, then there exists P in Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P)=roundedDotProduct(m,T). Here gamma(k,u)=(ku)/(1-ku) for natural k and real u; the hypothesis makes this denominator positive. The model contains u>=0 and r=m.round: R -> R with the property that for every real z there exists a real delta satisfying |delta|<=u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Tree(alpha) consists of finite nonempty ordered binary trees with alpha-labeled leaves, with no balance requirement. The depth is 0 at a leaf and 1+max(depth(L),depth(R)) at node(L,R). The exact sum is x at leaf(x) and exactSum(L)+exactSum(R) at node(L,R). For any real b, IsPerturbation(b,A,P) is the inductive relation requiring the same ordered binary shape: for corresponding leaves x,y it requires |y-x|<=b|x|, and for nodes it requires this relation on both corresponding children with the same b. Thus if T has leaf pairs (a_i,b_i), the existential P has corresponding leaves p_i with |p_i-a_i b_i|<=gamma(d+1,u)|a_i b_i|, and the exact sum of these p_i equals the actual rounded computation defined below. No perturbation of individual a_i or b_i is asserted.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). It maps each leaf (a,b) to leaf(ab), using exact real multiplication, and preserves every internal node and its left/right order: E(leaf((a,b)))=leaf(ab), E(node(L,R))=node(E(L),E(R)). It constructs a tree of separate products, with no internal-node arithmetic. E(T) is the reference tree in the target perturbation relation.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). For every model m and input tree T, it replaces each leaf (a,b) by leaf(r(ab)), where r=m.round, preserving all internal nodes and their left/right order. Explicitly Q_m(leaf((a,b)))=leaf(r(ab)) and Q_m(node(L,R))=node(Q_m(L),Q_m(R)), because m.mul(a,b)=r(ab). It performs no internal-node arithmetic. Its output is the input to roundedSum in roundedDotProduct. The depth smallness hypothesis is not required for this definition.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> R, defined for every model m and tree T as roundedSum(m,roundedProductTree(m,T)). For real-leaf trees, roundedSum(m,leaf(x))=x and roundedSum(m,node(L,R))=r(roundedSum(m,L)+roundedSum(m,R)), since m.add(a,b)=r(a+b). Equivalently D_m(leaf((a,b)))=r(ab) and D_m(node(L,R))=r(D_m(L)+D_m(R)). It performs one rounded multiplication per original leaf and one rounded addition per internal node, following the supplied tree. There is no additional leaf rounding after the product. Under (depth(T)+1)u<1, the target states that this actual result is the exact sum of a shape-preserving perturbation of exactProductTree(T), bounded at each leaf by gamma(depth(T)+1,u) times the absolute exact product.

assumptions: All factors, products, perturbed leaf values and arithmetic results lie in R. Input trees are arbitrary finite nonempty ordered binary trees of real pairs; no balance, uniform leaf depth, prescribed leaf count, or sign restriction on factors is assumed.

Every model contains a real u>=0 and a function r: R -> R satisfying: for every real z there exists a real delta with |delta|<=u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Delta may depend on z. Model addition and multiplication are r(a+b) and r(ab). No additional rounding-format or representability assumptions are supplied.
The theorem explicitly assumes (d+1)u<1, where d=depth(T) is natural and d+1 is interpreted in R for multiplication. Depth is 0 at a leaf and 1 plus the maximum child depth at a node.

The bound is gamma(d+1,u)=((d+1)u)/(1-(d+1)u), applied separately to each exact leaf product x as |y-x|<=gamma(d+1,u)|x|. A zero exact product must therefore remain zero in the perturbed tree. The existential object is a tree of real values, not pairs of perturbed factors.
